fields.summary: Autonomous plan run, no owner. The planner read the change set's intent (run 01M6W0Z45JXE stopped at wait-pr on a rebase conflict in seven files), internal/workflow/builtin/ship-change.toml, internal/api/ship_rebase.go (rebase, force-push with lease, rebase-conflict question), shipSettleConflict in internal/api/ship.go, the run engine's StopExit and the wait step's pass/timeout outcomes, and the model (milestone-25, wait-settles-conflicting-pr, ship-change-ci-fix-cycle). It picked milestone-25 as the served intent, as the CI-fix change set did. It raised one question with four topics: merge or rebase, who pushes the fixer's commit, what a design clash does, and the cap on fix cycles. The arbiter answered with Decision ship-merge-main-conflict-fixer: merge only, plain push, a conflicting merge is left in the worktree and the step fails to a conflict-fix agent step. The fixer resolves, regenerates goldens and rendered files, runs the touched packages' tests and commits with a Review: trailer, never pushing; the run's render and push step pushes and records. On a design clash the fixer aborts and raises a question that the run waits on. At most 3 cycles. The planner then worked out the wiring: wait steps have no fail outcome, so a conflicting wait settles and the green step routes there through a conflict triage. After land, a separate fixer step returns to rebase-merge, not render-pr, so nothing lands twice.
fields.title: Plan: ship-change merges main and fixes conflicts
